feedback: The candidate changes one controller value from the best raced design (iteration 1, score 163.8): kd 0.3 to 0.5, with kp 2.0, ki 0.02, base_speed 1.2, line_loss 'last_direction' and all sensing geometry and sensor_weights unchanged. The evidence is that line loss persisted at about 1 event per run after the sensing change (iteration 1: line_loss_events 1.1 on the oval, 1.0 on the s-bend and slalom), and max_error stayed at 0.061 to 0.064 m, the off-track limit. Raising kp to 2.5 in iteration 2 made the result worse (141.8), with more slalom line loss (1.85), so stronger proportional correction is not the fix. The kd change is a sound single-variable test of overshoot as the cause. Steering oscillation was 0.32 on the oval at kd 0.3, so it has some headroom before becoming the limit, but kd 0.5 may amplify the roughly 2 percent sensor noise. Speed is a secondary limit: base_speed 1.2 is below the roughly 1.5 m/s needed to finish in 3 s, and the one oval finish came with progress 0.70. Read the next race as follows. If line_loss_events falls to about 1 or below on the s-bend and slalom and max_error drops under about 0.06 m, derivative damping helped, so keep kd 0.5 and try a small kp reduction (for example 1.7) to test whether the correction is now too strong. If line loss stays near 1 and steering_oscillation rises above about 0.4, kd is amplifying noise, so return kd to 0.3 and change nothing else. If the robot tracks cleanly with progress stalling below full coverage, raise base_speed in small steps (1.2 to 1.4), since speed is then the limit.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events falls to about 1 or below on the s-bend and slalom with max_error under about 0.06 m, keep controller.kd at 0.5 and test controller.kp 1.7 alone, to check whether the correction is now too strong.

If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.4 or line loss does not improve, revert controller.kd to 0.3 (the best raced value) and change nothing else, because the derivative term may be amplifying the 2 percent sensor noise.

If the robot tracks cleanly on all tracks but progress stalls below full coverage, raise controller.base_speed in small steps (1.2 to 1.4) with kp 2.0 and kd at the best-performing value, since iteration 1 and 2 show speed is the next limit once line loss is controlled.
